item.title: Should the Las Vegas Raiders fire Rob Leonard?
item.description: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are leading the NFL in every defensive category you don’t want to be a part of. Total yards, Yards Per game, rushing yards, passing yards, total points and points per game. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard, in his first year, is taking some nasty lumps. While it appears that he shouldn’t be long for this job, the question begs: with the roster he currently has, who could do better and who would want to try? For the last six consecutive weeks, the Raiders’ defense has allowed 30+ points, a feat that hadn’t been replicated since the Jacksonville Jaguars did it in the 2020 season. No team in the modern era has ever allowed seven straight weeks of 30+ points allowed on defense. Additionally, allowing 150+ rushing yards to opposing teams in five of the last six weeks. While Raider Nation wants heads to roll, as they rightfully should, ask yourself: is it his fault? Keep it real Last season, the Raiders finished with the worst record in the NFL, which secured the number one overall draft selection. When Leonard took over, he was given old toilet water and asked to make wine. His best player, Maxx Crosby, was rehabbing a knee injury and the defensive backfield was completely overhauled through the 2026 draft. His best young defensive lineman, Tonka Hemingway, was still a largely unproven commodity who had done his best work in the weight room during the offseason. During that very same offseason, the Raiders finally invested in the linebacker position, bringing in Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker. Along with the former Eagles linebacker position coach. As for the defensive line, the group was largely ignored and it wasn’t until week 2 of the preseason that difference-maker Folorunso Fatukasi was brought in to help. Furthermore, there is only so much scheming you can do for an undersized defensive line against 12/13 personnel. Especially when they struggle to defend the run in regular 5/6-man sets to begin with. So how do you scheme when your guys aren’t playing up to their expectations and/or pay? Call outs Eric Stokes is supposed to be the leader of the defensive backs, but at this point, he could be cut outright from the team and they wouldn’t miss a beat. Outside of a streak or a fade, there isn’t a single pass route he excels at defending. When he takes the field, the opposing offenses look at him and salivate like they were staring at Kyu Blu Kelly last season. Somehow, mediocre play, prefaced as not giving up a passing touchdown because teams preferred to throw at a worse defensive back, got him a 3yr/$30M contract extension. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: 2027 CG commit Chase Branham signs with Indiana men’s basketball
item.description: Logan-Rogersville's Chase Branham (3) moves the ball during a Class 4 semifinal game against Vashon, Friday, March 20, 2026, at Mizzou Arena in Columbia, Mo. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It’s officially official, Chase Branham is an Indiana Hoosier. Branham, a combo guard in the class of who committed to Indiana men’s basketball way back in September 2025, signed his letter of intent with the program today, per an official release . He’s rated as a 4-star prospect by 247Sports , ranking in as the 5th highest-rated combo guard and 27th highest-rated prospect overall in the class of 2027. He’s the 10th highest-rated signing in program history, per 247Sports’ ratings. “Chase is a dynamic playmaker that is effective at all three levels,” head coach Darian DeVries said in the release. “Because of his work ethic and love for the game, he continues to push himself to new levels and has developed multi-dimensional skills. As good of a player that Chase is, he is an even better person and exemplifies all the attributes that we want our program to be about. It is exciting that Chase is officially a Hoosier and we cannot wait for him to get to Bloomington.” Branham originally chose Indiana over offers from Iowa, Purdue, Creighton, Missouri and Tennessee, among other programs. Branham was the first player in the class of 2027 to commit to the Hoosiers. He’s since been joined by 3-star German center Felix Kiehlneker and 5-star center Darius Wabbington . He originally attended Logan-Rogersville High School in Rogersville, Missouri, before transferring to La Lumiere School in La Porte, Indiana, for his final season of high school before joining Indiana. He’s the first La Lumiere player to sign with the in-state Hoosiers since Hanner Mosquera-Perea did as a member of the class of 2012. Branham averaged 21.5 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 2.2 steals per game as a junior for Logan-Rogersville, shooting 41.1% from 3-point range. item.description: Former Washington Commanders offensive coordinator Scott Turner joined the Trap or Dive Podcast this week for an in-depth film review of Washington’s offensive performance against the Los Angeles Rams. With a short turnaround ahead of Thursday night’s matchup against the New York Giants, the Commanders face another difficult defensive test—and one that could further expose the issues plaguing David Blough’s offense. According to SumerSports, both the Rams and Giants rank among the NFL’s top eight defenses in total EPA over the last four weeks, with New York sitting eighth. More importantly, the Giants present another significant challenge for Washington’s struggling offensive line. New York ranks fifth in pressure percentage and tenth in sack percentage, two categories that should concern anyone who watched the Commanders attempt to protect Jayden Daniels against Los Angeles. The Giants may not boast the same caliber of defensive talent Washington faced against the Rams, but the underlying concerns remain. If the Commanders fail to correct the protection breakdowns, inconsistent execution, and schematic shortcomings that defined Sunday’s loss, Thursday night could become another indictment of Dan Quinn and his coaching staff. If Washington loses to New York, the loud, dominating conversation will be how much longer owner Josh Harris is willing to tolerate the same recurring mistakes. So, what exactly went wrong against the Los Angeles Rams? Despite an encouraging start that saw Washington establish an early rhythm offensively, its efficiency deteriorated significantly as the game progressed. What initially appeared to be a promising offensive performance quickly unraveled into another frustrating display of missed assignments, poor technique, and an inability to sustain drives. Pass protection was problematic from the opening possession. Beyond the challenges of accounting for Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett, Washington’s offensive line struggled with its individual responsibilities. With Sam Cosmi as a notable exception, the unit repeatedly abandoned its technique, allowing defenders to win matchups that weren’t always the result of superior talent. While the protection plan deserves scrutiny, the film also revealed instances in which Washington’s linemen simply failed to execute their assignments. The running game presented a different set of problems, but the underlying theme was familiar: small details creating significant consequences. item.title: Dave Dombrowski signals an uncertain off-season ahead
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 29: Seiya Suzuki #27 of the Chicago Cubs bats against the San Diego Padres during the fourth inning in game one of the National League Wild Card Series at Petco Park on September 29, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) | Getty Images It does not appear as though the Phillies are going to pull off a major move at the GM Meetings this week in Las Vegas. It also appears they will not be alone. With the collective bargaining agreement set to expire on December 2, agents are fussing that teams do not want to make any major financial commitments yet without knowing what the rules in the new CBA are going to look like. Will there be a salary cap/floor? If not, what happens with the luxury tax? Will draft picks be allowed in trades? What will revenue sharing look like? But even if the Phils and Dombrowski don’t do anything substantive over the next couple of weeks, one would think he, and the rest of the front office decision makers, have formulated a plan on how to improve the roster and avoid “running it back” for yet another season. The team has clear needs in the outfield, bullpen, with starting pitching depth and utility infielder. They need to find a right-handed hitter for the middle of the lineup, and they need a late-inning left-handed relief pitcher. There are some high-end options to help in these areas. Adrian Morejon has been linked to the Phils as the top lefty reliever on the free agent market, and Seiya Suzuki and Randy Arozarena , two right-handed hitting outfielders who would solve their outfield/middle-of-the-order problems in one fell swoop, are obvious fits. But speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Dombrowski wondered aloud whether it would be in the team’s best interest to sign additional players already in their 30s to expensive, multi-year contracts ( quote via Phillies.com ). “We have a lot of high-end salary players, and they’re not young, they’re not old,” Dombrowski said. “But they’re in that age bracket that you have to make a decision. We maybe have enough high-end players, and you mean to complement them with other players overall. That’s a decision we have to make. But I’m not necessarily looking for our club to continue to get older, so you kind of factor all those things in and make a decision.” Dombrowski’s reluctance to sign another player entering his mid-30s to a deal that will see him earn close to $30 million a season at ages 35-37 is understandable. They’re already on the hook for big cash to Bryce Harper, Kyle Schwarber, Trea Turner and J.T. Realmuto, deals unlikely to age all that well in the coming years. Suzuki and Arozarena will be 33 in 2027. And if the Phillies are going to maintain a payroll similar to what they have over the last two years, they only have around $30 million to spend this off-season. item.title: The San Francisco Giants are the model for MLB’s salary cap
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 26: Logan Webb #62 of the San Francisco Giants adjusts his hat after giving up a double to Elly de la Cruz #44 of the Cincinnati Reds in the third inning at Oracle Park on August 26, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Yesterday, I dashed off a post about the bummer news regarding Harrison Bader’s status that had been reported out of the GM Meetings currently being held in Las Vegas. In it, I made mention of the owners’ latest proposal for a salary floor and cap, but I got a crucial figure wrong. After going back and looking at the offer more closely, it would appear that the sport has used the Giants as an example for just how competitive they want the most competitive team(s) in the sport to be. Another reason to be against the owners in this labor dispute. In their first proposal way back in May , owners pitched a floor of $171.2 million and a cap of $245.3 million, with the Competitive Balance Tax (CBT) figure being the basis. In other words, the cap number would be based on the average annual value of contracts — but not only the AAV. As with the current CBT calculation, the team’s contribution to the league’s health care plan for players is a part of the bottom line as is the mandatory contribution to the league’s pre-arbitration bonus pool that was negotiated into the most recent CBA. There’s not an exact publicly available figure for the health care contribution, but for 2026, it was an estimated $18 million per team. The mandatory pre-arb contribution is an annual fixed cost over the course of the CBA: $1.667 million. But the proposal also folds in two line items not currently factored into the CBT figure: amateur bonus pools. A team’s amateur draft figure and its international bonus pool would also become part of the salary cap math. Those figures can fluctuate year to year just based on free agent signings, trades, etc. What does this have to do with the Giants? By a stroke of luck, the Giants were awarded the fourth pick in the most recent MLB draft. They also traded away Patrick Bailey for Cleveland’s Competitive Balance pick. That increased their 2026 amateur draft bonus pool to $17.35 million. Their international draft figure was $5.44 million. That’s $22.79 million combined. Using Cot’s MLB Contracts, here i’s how the Giants’ would’ve looked under the May salary cap proposal in 2026: MLB roster (AAV): $204.53 million Amateur bonus pools (combined): $22.79 million Health care contribution: $18 million Pre-arbitration bonus pool: $1.67 million … Total: $246.99 million That’s, what, $10,000 under the first proposed salary cap? item.title: Arrowhead Pride Midseason Awards: The Chiefs’ top Defensive Rookie
item.description: (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs ’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Because the team’s bye came so early in Week 5, we have decided to move our annual awards to midseason. Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had one vote for our seven midseason awards, so nine votes will be tallied for each award. In this post, we’ll reveal our most improved player to this point in the season. CB Mansoor Delane VOTING: CB Mansoor Delane (8), DE R Mason Thomas (1) It took Mansoor Delane three defensive snaps to show why the Chiefs traded up to No. 6 overall to draft the former LSU star. On third-and-11 of the season’s opening drive, Delane picked off a Bo Nix pass intended for Courtland Sutton. A shoulder injury ended his NFL debut after that series, but he had already given Kansas City its first takeaway of the season in a pivotal matchup against the Denver Broncos . The interception was the highlight. In the next two games Delane played, he showed how much else he could give the defense. In road wins over the Miami Dolphins and Las Vegas Raiders , he recorded 10 tackles, seven of them solo, and a pass defended in each game. Some of an outside corner’s toughest snaps come when a runner gets to the perimeter, and the corner has to come downhill and make the tackle. Delane’s work in those situations has been an early strength of his game. Entering Week 8, his 81.6 run-defense grade from Pro Football Focus ranked ninth among cornerbacks. His coverage grades held up, too. Through Week 8, Delane’s 77.4 coverage grade led all rookie cornerbacks, while his 79.7 overall grade ranked fourth in PFF ’s rookie rankings. He defended five passes in five appearances. Second-round defensive end R Mason Thomas earned the other vote. He made an immediate impact against Denver, recording a sack in his NFL debut. Delane’s shoulder injury kept him out of the rematch with the Broncos and the win over the New York Jets, but his work in coverage and run support made him the clear choice at midseason. Cornerback was one of the biggest holes on Kansas City’s roster after the team lost All-Pro Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson in the same offseason. Delane has already helped ease that transition. Five appearances into his career, the Chiefs have seen him take away a third-down throw and do the less visible work of finishing plays when the ball comes his way on the ground. For a defense replacing two starting corners at once, that’s a promising start. Is Delane the Chiefs’ top defensive rookie so far this year? Let us know in the comments.

item.title: Juventus is targeting a loan move for Atalanta attacker
item.description: Juventus is targeting a loan move for Atalanta attacker Gianluca Scamacca is reportedly struggling to secure regular playing time at Atalanta this season, with competition for the centre-forward position affecting his involvement. His situation has attracted interest from Juventus, who are considering taking advantage of his circumstances to strengthen their attacking options in January. The Italian striker has found opportunities limited, with Nikola Krstović receiving the trust of Maurizio Sarri. Scamacca has therefore struggled to establish himself as a regular starter, raising questions about his future in Bergamo. Juventus, meanwhile, are still searching for greater consistency from their attacking options despite signing two new forwards during the summer transfer window. Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani have yet to provide everything the Bianconeri want from their frontline , and the club remains interested in adding another striker. Juventus consider a January move for Scamacca Scamacca has struggled to make the desired impression at Atalanta and faces strong competition for opportunities. His playing style also appears not to fit comfortably into Sarri’s current system, potentially making a departure an option for the club. Juventus believe they could benefit from his situation and see him as a forward capable of improving their attacking options. They consider him a suitable profile for Luciano Spalletti, who would welcome additional quality and depth in the final third. According to Tuttojuve , the Bianconeri are considering a loan move for Scamacca in January, with an option to make the transfer permanent at the end of the season. Such an agreement would allow Juventus to assess his performances before committing to a permanent transfer, while also giving the striker an opportunity to revive his career with another Italian club. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Scamacca emerges as an alternative to Icardi Juventus have also been linked with Mauro Icardi , but there are concerns surrounding his current situation. He has not played football since the end of last season, which could make his immediate availability a consideration. Scamacca offers a different proposition, particularly because he is younger and could provide a longer-term option for the club. item.description: Maybe you’ve heard that Penn State Wrestling is good. Really good. Record-settingly good. Again . Again . And they are expected to dominate again this season. You’d really like to check it out, but you didn’t wrestle and have no idea how it works. It doesn’t look anything like that male-targeted soap opera where people leap from turnbuckles and inexplicably use foreign objects! Lucky for you, this is one of the best wrestling communities on the internet. And we’ve got your back. Here I’m going to go over the basics of “folkstyle” wrestling (the kind done by scholastic wrestlers in the United States): the positions, how to score, and some basic terminology. Since this is a Penn State blog, we will be focusing on college rules and scoring; youth and high school wrestling are similar but use slightly different rules (usually shorter period lengths and no riding time). The two types of international wrestling (Freestyle and Greco-Roman) differ more substantially , but still share a lot of the same moves. The Structure Event Types There are two main types of wrestling competition: standard tournaments and dual meets (team vs team), but each is composed of a number of one-on-one matches between two wrestlers of near equal weight. We will cover the overall team scoring for both forms of competition near the end, but until then we will be focusing on what happens during a single match. Weight Classes In NCAA wrestling, there are 10 weight classes, each designated by the maximum weight allowed. Wrestlers are weighed a couple hours before competition begins and can weigh no more than the stated weight. For multi-day tournaments, wrestlers generally have to weigh-in each day, but may be allowed to exceed the limit by a couple of pounds on subsequent days. There is a blanket allowance of one-pound for both teams if either team had a dual within the past 48 hours. A match can end early by a wrestler pinning their opponent by holding both of their shoulder blades against the mat for one second (a pin or fall) or exhibiting “technical mastery” by building a lead of 15+ points (a technical fall). If the match is tied after 7 minutes, there are overtime periods ( described later ). Each wrestler is assigned either red or green prior to the match for scoring purposes. Patriots fans should still expect Brown to sit out, with the bye the following week and getting a close to fully healthy Brown for Week 12 being much more important than rushing him back in Week 10. item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle Derrick Harmon is carted off the field against the Cleveland Browns on Oct, 1, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers are opening the 21-day practice window for defensive tackle Derrick Harmon on Wednesday, head coach Mike McCarthy announced on Wednesday, as Harmon returns from the injured reserve. Harmon, 23, has been out for a month with a left foot injury. He left the team’s Oct. 1 game against the Cleveland Browns and was carted off the field. He was later seen wearing a protective boot on his injured foot and was placed on injured reserve on Monday, Oct. 5. This is the first week that Harmon is eligible to return from the injured reserve list, having missed four games. With Harmon out of the lineup, the Steelers have had to lean heavily on Keeanu Benton and Yahya Black , alongside veteran Cam Heyward, on their defensive front, and rookies Gabriel Rubio and Kevin Jobity Jr. have also contributed more than expected with both Harmon and veteran Sebastian Joseph-Day out with injuries. The surprisingly strong play of the young Steelers has allowed the team to continue to dominate as run stuffers. The Steelers are currently third in the league in run defense, allowing 83.9 yards per game, just behind the San Francisco 49ers (80.9) and Tampa Bay Buccaneers (79.1). The Steelers will need to clear a spot on their 53-man roster in order to make space for Harmon’s return from injured reserve. item.title: Shrewsbury 'hit all the boxes' for new owners - Friedel
item.description: Shrewsbury Town are 15th in League Two [Getty Images] Shrewsbury Town's new sporting director Brad Friedel says the club is the perfect project for the US-backed owners after a Europe-wide search ended with them taking contol of the League Two outfit. Scott Davidson's Biscayne ST LLC consortium, which Friedel is part of, completed their takeover on Monday, buying 87.4% of the shares and allowing long-time owner Roland Wycherley to relinquish control. "Scott and I met through friends in Miami and through the love of football and nothing more or less," former Blackburn and USA goalkeeper Friedel told BBC Radio Shropshire in an exclusive interview. "As we got to know each other, our thoughts on business and football aligned - we got to the point where we said let's try to find a club which fits a whole bunch of criteria. "So we looked in Turkey, Poland, Portugal and Holland but the clubs we were looking at, something didn't align for one reason or another and a lot of it came down to did we think our group can help the football club because we want to bring the town firmly behind the club." Wycherley first announced his plans to find a successor five years ago and Friedel says with Davidson already being a majority shareholder of Edinburgh-based The Spartans in Scottish League Two, they wanted a club they could take forward both on and off the field. "The one-town club really appealed to us because we want to integrate the club even more into the town than it is now and when you look at the investment going into the EFL, the foreign investment going into it, there's a reason for it because there's no better place for football than the United Kingdom. "Once we decided our group would be best suited to the UK market, Shrewsbury hit all the boxes of what we like, but also what we feel we can deliver towards the club and the town." "I don't look at football anymore as I would only take a job in the Premier League or the Champions League," he said.
